luna-lighthouse.title: Luna and the Lighthouse on the Moon
luna-lighthouse.summary: When the moon’s lighthouse goes dark, a small purple dragon has to find a big light.

pages.0: High above the sleepy Earth, on the quiet silver moon, stood a tall lighthouse with a candy-striped roof. Every night its golden light swept across the sky, so that lost stars could find their way home.
pages.1: Luna was a small purple dragon with a crooked crown and a very big heart. She lived at the bottom of the lighthouse, in a round room full of pillows and moon-dust.
pages.2: One night, the golden light flickered… and went out. Far away, a baby star began to cry. “I can’t see the way home!” it called into the dark.
pages.3: Luna looked up at the cold, dark lamp. She could ask the racing comets for help, or she could try something she had never, ever done before.
pages.4a: Luna flapped to the edge of the moon and waved at the comets zooming by. “Please,” she said, “lend me a little of your light.” The comets giggled and swirled around the lighthouse like glowing ribbons.
pages.5a: Round and round they flew, until the lamp began to shine again, brighter than ever. The baby star followed the ribbons all the way home. “Thank you, Luna!” it twinkled.
pages.4b: Luna climbed all ninety-nine steps to the very top. She took a deep breath, puffed out her cheeks and… whoosh! A tiny, warm flame curled into the lamp.
pages.5b: The lighthouse glowed purple and gold, the most beautiful light the moon had ever seen. The baby star followed it all the way home, and Luna learned that small dragons can make big light.
pages.6: Back in her pillow room, Luna yawned a sleepy dragon yawn. Outside, the light kept sweeping gently across the sky. Goodnight, Luna. Goodnight, little stars.

choice.prompt: How should Luna bring the light back?

tiger-roar.title: The Tiger Who Forgot His Roar
tiger-roar.summary: Raja wakes up and his roar comes out as a squeak. The whole jungle helps him find it.

pages.0: Raja the tiger stretched his enormous paws, opened his mouth wide, and ROARED. Except it wasn’t a roar at all. It was a tiny little… squeak.
pages.1: The parrot laughed so hard she fell off her branch. “Your roar is missing!” she squawked. “Let’s go and find it!”
pages.2: They looked under the banana leaves. They looked behind the waterfall. They even looked inside the sleepy hippo’s ear, which he did not enjoy one bit.
pages.3: At last, a little frog hopped up. “I borrowed it,” he whispered. “I wanted to be loud, just once.” Raja smiled. “Then let’s be loud together!”
pages.4: So Raja and the frog took a big breath and ROARED and CROAKED at the very same time. The whole jungle cheered, and even the hippo wiggled his ears.

pip-cloud-whales.title: Captain Pip and the Cloud Whales
pip-cloud-whales.summary: A tiny sky-pirate follows a song through the clouds and makes the biggest friends in the sky.

pages.0: Captain Pip was the smallest sky-pirate in the floating city, but she had the biggest telescope. Every morning she searched the clouds for adventure.
pages.1: One morning she heard a song, low and gentle, like a lullaby hummed by the wind. “Full sails!” cried Pip, and her paper boat lifted into the sky.
pages.2: Through the pink clouds she sailed, past the rainbow bridge, until she saw them: whales made of cloud, singing as they swam through the sky.
pages.3: The smallest whale was stuck in a knot of thunder. Pip tied a rope to her boat, pulled with all her might, and… pop! The little whale was free.
pages.4: That night the cloud whales sang Pip all the way home. And every morning since, when you hear the wind hum, that’s them saying good morning to her.

beep-garden.title: Beep and the Garden of Stars
beep-garden.summary: A curious little robot learns how stars are born, and plants a constellation of its own.

pages.0: Beep was a tiny round robot who looked after a garden at the very edge of space. Every day Beep watered the moon-flowers and asked one big question: where do stars come from?
pages.1: The wise old comet explained that stars are born inside giant clouds of gas and dust called nebulas, where gravity pulls everything together until it gets hot enough to shine.
pages.2: So Beep gathered stardust from the garden paths, packed it into a glowing seed, and planted it in the softest, darkest patch of sky.
pages.3: Beep waited, and watered, and waited some more. Stars take millions of years to grow, the comet reminded, but a gardener must always begin somewhere.
pages.4: That night, Beep arranged the brightest seeds into the shape of a watering can. Now, if you look up very carefully, you might just see Beep’s constellation smiling back.

luna-sleepy-comet.title: Luna and the Sleepy Comet
luna-sleepy-comet.summary: A tired little comet can’t keep flying, so Luna finds the coziest crater on the moon for a nap.

pages.0: One quiet night, Luna was polishing the stars by the lighthouse when something went wobble, wobble, bump! A little comet named Zoom had tumbled onto the moon.
pages.1: “I’m so tired,” yawned Zoom. “I’ve been flying round and round the sky all week, and my tail won’t sparkle anymore.” Its glow was as dim as a sleepy candle.
pages.2: Luna knew exactly what to do. She found the softest crater on the moon, filled it with moon-dust pillows, and tucked Zoom in under a blanket of starlight.
pages.3: Then she hummed the lullaby her grandmother used to sing, soft and slow, like waves on a silver sea. Zoom’s eyes grew heavy, and heavier, and closed.
pages.4: In the morning, Zoom woke up as bright as a firework. “Hop on!” it laughed, and it gave Luna the fastest, happiest ride all the way around the moon. Goodnight, Zoom. Goodnight, Luna.

luna-moon-garden.title: Luna’s Silver Garden
luna-moon-garden.summary: Luna plants tiny seeds that only grow in moonlight, and learns that the best things take time.

pages.0: Luna found a pouch of tiny silver seeds hidden behind the lighthouse door. A note inside said: “Plant me in moonlight. Be patient. I will glow.”
pages.1: So Luna dug small holes in the soft moon-dust and planted every seed. She watered them with dew from the comets and waited… and waited. Nothing happened.
pages.2: “Maybe they don’t like me,” Luna sighed. But every night she sang to the seeds and told them stories about the stars, just in case they were listening.
pages.3: On the seventh night, a tiny silver sprout peeked out. Then another, and another, until the whole garden was full of little leaves that shimmered like frost.
pages.4: Soon the flowers opened, glowing soft and white, lighting a path for every traveler in the night sky. And Luna learned that the most beautiful things are worth waiting for.

pip-rainbow-map.title: Captain Pip and the Rainbow Map
pip-rainbow-map.summary: A map painted in seven colors leads Pip on a treasure hunt across the sky.

pages.0: A gust of wind blew a strange map right into Captain Pip’s paws. It wasn’t drawn in ink. It was painted in stripes of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
pages.1: “Each color is a clue!” cried Pip. The red stripe led to a cloud shaped like a strawberry. The orange stripe pointed to a sunset lighthouse. The yellow one hid in a field of sunflowers floating in the sky.
pages.2: Green, blue and indigo took her over a forest, across a river of mist and through a tunnel of evening sky. At last, the violet stripe ended at a tiny wooden chest.
pages.3: Pip opened it with a gasp. Inside there was no gold, only seeds. Thousands of seeds, and a note: “Treasure grows when you share it.”
pages.4: So Pip sailed home and gave seeds to everyone in the floating city. By spring, every rooftop bloomed with flowers, and the city had never been so rich.

pip-thunder-drum.title: Captain Pip and the Thunder Drum
pip-thunder-drum.summary: The thunder keeps the floating city awake, until Pip meets the lonely giant who plays it.

pages.0: Boom! Boom! BOOM! Every night the thunder rolled over the floating city, and nobody could sleep. The babies cried, the cats hid, and even the moon looked grumpy.
pages.1: Captain Pip put on her bravest hat and sailed right into the dark clouds. There, sitting on a storm cloud, was a giant with a huge silver drum.
pages.2: “Why do you drum so loudly?” asked Pip. The giant looked down at his boots. “Because it’s lonely up here,” he said, “and loud drumming makes me feel less alone.”
pages.3: Pip had an idea. She taught the giant to drum softly, pitter-patter, like rain on a roof. Then she brought her whole crew to sing along with him.
pages.4: Now, every night, the giant plays a gentle rain-song, and the whole floating city falls asleep to it. And the giant is never lonely, because Pip visits every Sunday.

beep-moon-faces.title: Beep and the Moon’s Many Faces
beep-moon-faces.summary: Why does the moon change shape? Beep finds out with a lamp and a ball.

pages.0: Every night, Beep watched the moon from the garden at the edge of space. Sometimes it was a thin smile, sometimes half a cookie, and sometimes a big round plate. “Is the moon shrinking?” Beep wondered.
pages.1: The wise old comet chuckled. “The moon never changes size,” it said. “And it doesn’t make its own light. It shines because the sun lights it up, like a flashlight shining on a ball.”
pages.2: Beep tried it with a lamp and a ball. The sun always lights exactly half of the moon. But as the moon travels around the Earth, we see different amounts of that bright half.
pages.3: When the lit side faces us, we see a full moon. When it faces away, we see almost nothing: a new moon. In between come the crescents and the half moons.
pages.4: The whole journey takes about twenty-nine and a half days. So Beep made a moon calendar, and every night Beep draws the moon’s face and says, “Goodnight, moon. See you tomorrow, in a brand new shape.”

beep-rainbow-recipe.title: Beep and the Rainbow Recipe
beep-rainbow-recipe.summary: Beep discovers the secret ingredients of a rainbow: sunlight, raindrops and the right place to stand.

pages.0: After a rain shower, a rainbow stretched across Beep’s garden. “I want to make one too!” said Beep. “But what is a rainbow made of?”
pages.1: The comet explained, “Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mix of many colors. When sunlight passes through a raindrop, it bends and bounces, and the colors spread apart.”
pages.2: Beep wrote down the recipe: one bright sun, lots of tiny raindrops, and one important rule. The sun must be behind you, and the raindrops in front of you.
pages.3: So Beep stood with the sun at its back and sprayed a fine mist from its watering-can arm. And there it was, a tiny rainbow: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
pages.4: From that day on, Beep made a little rainbow every sunny morning, just to say hello to the colors hiding inside the light.

raja-banana-race.title: Raja and the Great Banana Race
raja-banana-race.summary: Raja wants to win the jungle race, but a friend in trouble changes everything.

pages.0: The jungle was having its Great Banana Race, and the prize was the biggest, yellowest banana anyone had ever seen. Raja the tiger stretched his enormous paws. “I’m going to win!” he roared.
pages.1: Ready, steady, GO! Raja zoomed ahead of the monkey, the parrot and even the speedy little mouse. He was so fast that his stripes looked blurry.
pages.2: But halfway there, Raja heard a small voice. The tortoise was stuck on his back in the mud, waving his legs like an upside-down table. “Help!” he giggled. “I’m upside down!”
pages.3: Raja stopped, rolled the tortoise over and gave him a ride on his back. Then the monkey fell in a puddle, so Raja carried her too, and then the parrot, and then the mouse.
pages.4: Raja crossed the finish line last, with the whole jungle riding on his back. Everybody cheered, and they cut the giant banana into pieces so every single friend got a slice. Winning together tasted the sweetest.
